questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The factory supplies electrical components ____ cars.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'for'. The preposition "for" is used to indicate the purpose or intended recipient of something. In the sentence "The factory supplies electrical components for cars," the word "for" indicates that the electrical components are provided with the specific purpose of being used in cars. This preposition shows the relationship between the action ("supplies") and its purpose ("cars"). Other prepositions are not correct for the given context. "Above" generally indicates a higher position or level in space. "Among" is used to indicate being part of a group or surrounded by something. "Upon" typically denotes a spatial or temporal relationship, meaning "on" or "at the time of." Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The factory supplies electrical components for cars.

NOTE:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.

The concert tickets were bought by my friend.
options_en: My friend has bought the concert tickets.
My friend bought the concert tickets.
My friend buys the concert tickets.
My friend is buying the concert tickets.
questions.solution_en:
• The given sentence is in passive voice (The concert tickets were bought by my friend).

• To convert to active voice, we need subject + verb + object:

o Subject: "My friend"

o Verb: "bought" (past tense of "were bought")

o Object: "the concert tickets"

Other options:

• (1) My friend has bought the concert tickets. → Incorrect, as it changes the tense to present perfect.

• (3) My friend buys the concert tickets. → Incorrect, as it changes the tense to simple present.

• (4) My friend is buying the concert tickets. → Incorrect, as it changes the tense to present continuous.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

She said, "it is too good to be true".
options_en: She said it were too good to be true.
She said that it was too good to be true.
She is saying that it is too good to be true.
She says that it is too good to be true.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject + V1 + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said' will be changed to 'said that'.

'Is' will be changed to 'was'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): She said that it was too good to be true.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The incident is orchestrated by a pro. Finding the person behind it is begun by the owner.
options_en: A pro orchestrates the incident. The owner begins finding the person behind it.
A pro orchestrated the incident. The owner began finding the person behind it.
A pro orchestrates the incident. The owner began finding the person behind it.
A pro is orchestrating the incident. The owner begins finding the person behind it.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" ('is' in this case) verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Indefinite tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V1/V5 + Object.

For example:

You are liked by her. (Passive Voice)

She likes you. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Jake thought no one knew how much he liked Julie, but his face when he got to know that she'll be at the party really _______!
questions.solution_en:
'Get it done' (achieve; accomplish) results in a grammatical error (according to the Subject-Verb Agreement principle, we need a singular verb with a singular noun/subject 'his face'; while 'get' is a plural verb); 'gave him away' (showed someone's secret feelings); 'got over it' (recovered from some physical or mental ailment); and 'got a word in edgeways' (to speak or express one's opinion despite other people dominating the conversation). Among these options, only 'gave him away' is grammatically correct and at the same time, results in a meaningful sentence/idea - 'his secret feelings for Julie were evident on his face when Jake got to know that she'll be there'.

The answer is option (b).

Note:

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - She likes cooking. [singular subject and verb] -- They like to cook vegetables. [plural subject and verb]
